newsitem.title: ITALY: Mediaset still aims for 3rd licence-chairman.
newsitem.headline: Mediaset still aims for 3rd licence-chairman.

text.p: Italian TV and advertising group Mediaset still aims to participate in the competition for the licence to operate Italy's third mobile telecoms network, the group's chairman Fedele Confalonieri said on Monday.

The company's largest shareholder and leader of the centre-right opposition in parliament, ex-prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, had said last Thursday: "I know for certain that it (Mediaset) will not participate".

Confalonieri said while attending a conference in Milan referring to Berlusconi, "Certainly, he was misunderstood, his comments were political reflections" inspired by the lack of confidence about obtaining the licence from the "centre-left government".

Confalonieri added regarding Mediaset: "We have still the intention of competing for the third licence with the consortium that we have put in place together with our partners...Certainly, we have a perplexing problem because every day that passes reinforces the position of groups already in the sector while it weakens the position of those who have yet to enter".
He stressed that Mediaset was not even considering pulling out of its fixed-line telecom Albacom venture, which it shares with with state-controlled bank BNL and British Telecommunications.
Berlusconi's private company Fininvest has a near half share in Mediaset after shares in Mediaset were floated on the bourse last year.

The competition for Italy's third mobile phone licence is scheduled for this year with the successful bidder set to join other operators -- the state-contolled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and the Omnitel consortium, where the biggest shareholder is Olivetti.
